then.text: Mind how you go. And the cream: float it, never stir.
Cream from the farm and brown sugar from the duty free. Now. Show me you were listening.
What goes into the warmed glass first?

Float it over the back of a spoon

then.text: Hot through the cold. That's it, exactly as Joe Sheridan made it in 1943. Taste that.
Here, something came out of the steam while you were stirring. It seems to have taken a liking to you.

else.text: Ah, no. Joe Sheridan is turning in his grave. Come back and try again.
Ice? Milk? In an Irish coffee? Away with you and try again.
Not first, no. Have another think and come back to me.
Not first, no. Have another think and come back to me.
Lovely cream. Now brown sugar: the duty-free shop at Shannon Airport, the first duty free in the world. Ask for the good stuff.
Cream first. Golden Vale cream, from the dairy farm north of the river. Lightly whipped, mind.
This is where Irish coffee was invented, did you know? 1943. A flying boat to America turned back in a winter storm, and Joe Sheridan, the chef, warmed the passengers up.
A passenger asked was it Brazilian coffee. 'No,' says Joe, 'that's Irish coffee.' I make it the same way. Will you help me make a proper one?
I need cream from the dairy farm north of the river, and brown sugar from the duty free at Shannon Airport.

foynes_curator.text: The flying boats came in from 1937. Pan Am's Yankee Clipper, the Boeing 314, carried seventy-odd passengers in luxury: a dining room, beds, a honeymoon suite at the back.
In 1939 the first scheduled passenger flights across the Atlantic landed here. The radio and weather room upstairs is how it was, all valves and Morse.

foynes_pilot.text: Navigating a flying boat across the Atlantic was dead reckoning and star sights. You'd take a sextant to the window and pray for a gap in the clouds.
Coming home to Foynes on the Shannon at dawn was the loveliest sight in the world. The water flat as a plate. Then breakfast.
